messages:
zoe: Heads-up — saw router pool hit queue capacity and several clients received 503s for ~3m. One org was responsible for most of it. We need a short plan: sample/shed telemetry, eviction strategy (per-key bloom vs priority), and whether we prefer 429 vs 503 when shedding.

mike: Curious — are these 503s coming from upstream (edge) or from the router rejecting at accept time?

zoe: From the router gateway, before it forwards to model workers. We hit queue_capacity and our accept handler returned 503. infra-bot posted alerts: router-3 Q>95% multiple times.

infra-bot: alert: router-3 queue_depth=96% (avg 30s), region=us-west, triggered at 1798765410.

ali: Agree we should avoid blanket 503s for single noisy org. Proposal: per-org soft-cap + per-key burst buckets. When per-org soft-cap exceeded, start spilling least-priority keys and return 429 for those keys; only return 503 when cluster-wide capacity exhausted.

sam: :+1: Also need sampled shed request bodies/headers (5-10%) so we can debug hot callers without logging everything. Tag samples with trace_id and org_id.

zoe: Sketch of limiter config I was playing with:
```json
{
  "per_org_soft": 80,
  "per_org_hard": 120,
  "per_key_burst": 25,
  "queue_capacity": 1000,
  "priority_eviction": true,
  "eviction_policy": "least_recent_high_cost"
}
```
If soft breached -> 429 on low-priority keys; if hard breached -> return 503 for new accepts.

mike: A few edge cases: long-lived streaming requests tie up slots differently (KV cache growth). We should weight cost by estimated remaining tokens so eviction is cost-aware.

jess: For telemetry: emit metrics: `router.queue_length`, `router.shed_rate{reason}`, `router.429_vs_503_ratio`, `router.evicted_keys` and a histogram of `estimated_remaining_tokens`. Console should surface these per-org + per-model.

sam: UX ask: console toggle for "emergency per-org throttle" with a short-acting override and a mandatory notes field (who, why, duration). Also show live top-5 keys by token-rate so SEs can reach out.

ali: On 429 vs 503 semantics: 429 means "you are over client quota" (client should retry/Backoff). 503 means "service overloaded" — we want 429 when shedding by policy (per-org/key) and 503 only when global capacity is exhausted or degraded. That aligns with clients implementing exponential backoff on 429.

zoe: TL;DR: implement soft/hard per-org caps, cost-weighted priority eviction, sample shed requests (trace+org), and expose metrics + console controls. Can someone take the limiter PR and add metrics?

mike: I can pick up limiter PR. Will add `estimated_remaining_tokens` weighting and a shed-sampling hook.

jess: I'll add the new metrics to the metrics repo and create dashboard panels: per-org queue depth + 429/503 split + top evicted keys.

ops-bot: FYI: created incident runbook stub "router-overload" and linked it to oncall when queue>90%. Please review: https://internal/ops/runbooks/router-overload

ali: One more: add a short-lived sample store for shed traces (30d TTL), and mark samples as PII-filtered. We should avoid storing full inputs unless approved.

zoe: Good call. For now, configure sampling at 5% with PII redaction. We'll iterate. I'll open a design doc and tag @mike @jess to coordinate PRs. :rocket:

mike: Working on PR now, will include unit tests for eviction ordering and a small loadtest script.

sam: Can we also add a quick CLI to trigger a per-org emergency throttle for support? Helpful during incidents.

zoe: Yup — add an API endpoint guarded by RBAC and audit logs.

jess: Putting dashboard draft in PR and sharing in #eng-platform for feedback.

zoe: Thanks all — let's reconvene async. If you run into config tradeoffs ping me.
